no6.summary: The Marquis del Vasto to Charles V from Rome, early December 1527, after the agreement for the Pope's liberty: his plan to take the army out of Rome toward Tuscany, secure Siena, threaten Florence, take Perugia and the state of Urbino and pass into the Marche, with the warning that the army cannot be sustained 'desta manera' without money. prior/BnF_fr3022_f16_decryption.txt is George Lasry's preliminary letter-level decryption (cryptiana GL.htm), which also serves as the sign transcription; texts/no6_decryption.txt is this project's current reading of the cipher runs with the code groups identified (98.0% of 1,680 tokens), and n6_reading.md its edited text of 18 Sept.
no6.en:
I believe this is more likely, because, according to the [dnh], they will not follow it in coming so far
forward, since there is no army of theirs remaining in Lombardy strong enough to resist a large band of Germans that the
King of Hungary could, by Your Majesty's order, send down into Italy. And if that happened, and they found themselves so
far advanced, I believe they would find it hard to go back, and harder still to stay and [bnq], and in the end they could
only expect great loss; and for this reason I think they will want first to finish the business of Lombardy rather than
take another road.

And … is to win [rar] on the way and put it under Your Majesty's command, which in these times is […] that one must most
work to finish, since it will suffice to sustain the army, which is the most important thing, and the one Your Majesty
must most desire.

system: Caesar-shifted substitution (+1) over a 21-letter alphabet with homophones, three-letter b-/c-/d- code groups, and two-per-syllable code signs (Lasry's 'Gasto-Charles V Cipher 2').
